text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] ap-southeast-1: ELB target health spike + 502s across inference-gateway-prod (p95 latency > 3s) — pager duty invoked. link: https://alerts.redwood.example/4001234567

maya (oncall): seeing it in the dashboard, lots of 502/504s coming from elb-apse1-frontends. Uptime page shows region-wide target group flapping. Starting triage.

sam (sre): +1, can we confirm if Route53 weighted routing changed? pinging jin and aaron to check infra/network side.

jin (infra): I can see increased connection resets at the LB layer and a subset of instances marking UNHEALTHY. No EBS detach events in CloudTrail. NLB->ELB handshake resets at ~10:30 UTC.

maya (oncall): customers reporting degraded API throughput, some timeouts. Running initial impact calc: ~18% of production requests are failing or timing out over the last 10m.

aaron (neteng): route53 health checks are green; however, ASG scale-ins yesterday left a few hosts in a different subnet. Suspect asymmetric egress path to NAT gateways in ap-southeast-1a.

leah (prod-eng): can we quick-roll to the fallback model-server pool in ap-southeast-2 while we investigate? That buys time.

sam (sre): agree. Plan: 1) reweight Route53 to shift 60% traffic to ap-southeast-2, 2) temporarily increase ELB connection draining to 120s, 3) mark suspected subnets out of rotation. Who can run the DNS weight change?

jin (infra): I can perform the Route53 change. Executing now — will update when propagated.

ops-bot: Route53 change: set inference-api.redwood.ai weights: ap-southeast-1 -> 40, ap-southeast-2 -> 60. Change-id: r53-4001234567. Propagation ETA ~30s.

maya (oncall): rolling 60% now. Observability: latency p50 unchanged, p95 dropping slightly in 2m. Errors trending down to ~8%. Good sign.

aaron (neteng): digging into VPC flow logs — seeing a spike in retransmits from a specific ENI pool in ap-southeast-1b. Likely overloaded NAT/egress. Opening a ticket with cloud provider in parallel.

leah (prod-eng): verifying model statefulness across pools — sessions are sticky but we have KV sync. Some requests may get a slight cold-start in ap-southeast-2. Acceptable tradeoff.

sam (sre): maya, please start incident bridge and notify customer-facing teams. Use the incident runbook: REGION_NETWORK_DEGRADATION.

maya (oncall): creating bridge now — conf: https://meet.redwood.example/incident-4001234567. Pager rotations informed. Creating #incident-4001234567 channel and posting summary.

incident-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-4001234567. Severity: Sev2. Incident commander: maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): temporary mitigations applied: Route53 weights changed, draining increased, and instances in suspected subnets marked OutOfService. Monitoring for error rate recovery.

jin (infra): stack checks: no recent kernel upgrades, no EBS throttling. ELB metrics show healthy_target_percent improving after drain. Suspect region NIC/ENI saturation to provider side. Raising provider case: case-PRV-821.

leah (prod-eng): can we add a fallback routing policy to send read-only queries to cached edge? Might reduce load.

sam (sre): yes — enable edge-cache-only for non-write endpoints. leah, please produce the patch and I will deploy to the edge routing rule.

leah (prod-eng): patch posted, deploying to canary: /deploy edge-route-cache v1.2.3-canary.

ops-bot: Deploy started: edge-route-cache v1.2.3-canary by leah. Canary targets: 5%.

maya (oncall): error rate down to ~3% after DNS reweight + edge cache + drain. Customer impact reduced but still visible for a small subset.

aaron (neteng): provider responded: they see packet loss originating in fabric for ap-southeast-1b affecting NAT/egress; they're working a fix. ETA unknown. We should prepare for multi-hour mitigation.

sam (sre): long term plan: expand capacity in ap-southeast-2, and as a safety, prepare a cross-region session-restore story if we need full failover. For now, keep weights at 60/40 until provider confirms.

maya (oncall): noted. I'm looping in support to escalate to top-tier for impacted customers. Posting public status update draft.

leah (prod-eng): draft status: "We are investigating elevated errors for customers in ap-southeast-1. Traffic has been partially shifted to a healthy region to restore service; some latency and errors may persist. We will update in 15 minutes." Ping me for edits.

incident-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/4001234567 — initial message posted.

maya (oncall): provider sent a patch to routing fabric — they started mitigation at 10:58 UTC. Seeing immediate reduction in retransmits for a subset of ENIs. Monitoring.

sam (sre): let's prepare a rollback of Route53 weights if the provider fix causes asymmetric load or instability. jin, can you automate a quick switch?

jin (infra): yes — I created a runbook script: scripts/r53-reweight.sh. Manual approval required. Keeping it handy.

ops-bot: Canary deploy of edge-route-cache succeeded. Edge error-rate for read endpoints down 70%.

maya (oncall): last check: overall error rate back to baseline (~0.5%), p95 latency near normal. Provider confirms partial fabric fix, still monitoring.

aaron (neteng): marking ENI pool ap-southeast-1b as degraded in our internal inventory to prevent autoscaling into it until provider confirms.

leah (prod-eng): rolling back canary to full deploy to maximize cache coverage — deploying edge-route-cache v1.2.3 to 100%.

incident-bot: edge-route-cache v1.2.3 deploy to 100% complete.

maya (oncall): moving to post-incident activities: collect timelines, customer impact numbers, and runbook gaps. We'll keep the incident channel open for 1h for follow-up. If no regressions, we'll close.

sam (sre): action items: 1) confirm provider closure/cause, 2) add automated ENI health alarms + runbook update for route53 weights, 3) review autoscaling subnet tagging to avoid cross-subnet drift.

jin (infra): logging provider case updates to infra-ticket-400123. Also scheduling a postmortem meeting.

maya (oncall): thanks all. Final note: Great cross-team response — the partial DNS reweight + edge cache combo is a good mitigation pattern to codify. Closing active mitigation.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to monitoring. Channel will remain for follow-ups.

maya (oncall): (closing note) final customer impact: 18% requests affected at peak, ~90% recovered within 12 minutes after mitigation, no data loss. Postmortem invite sent.
